data.cultural_impact: The name Manivel holds significant importance in the Tamil Nadu region of India, where Lord Murugan, also known as Manivel, is a widely revered deity. He is believed to be the god of wealth, and his name itself representations the symbolic union of a precious jewel (Mani) and a powerful weapon (Vel). Thus, the name Manivel is deeply rooted in the cultural traditions and beliefs of the Tamil people.
data.spiritual_significance: For Hindus, the name Manivel is not just a mere label but a manifestation of Lord Murugan. It carries with it the divine blessings of the god, who is known to bestow prosperity, wealth, and success upon his devotees. The name signifies the presence of prosperity, abundance, and protection in one's life. It serves as a constant reminder of Lord Murugan's compassion and love towards his followers. Therefore, for those bearers of the name Manivel, it is a spiritual source of strength, inspiration, and good fortune.

historical_references.reference: Manivel Thirumugatambidaan, a Jaina hermit who lived during the Sangam period (approximately 2nd century BCE to 4th century CE) in Tamil Nadu, India, is believed to have authored a work known as 'Agastya Samhita'. This text is considered one of the Agama scriptures in Jainism, detailing the rituals, dogmas, and conduct of Jain monks and nuns. Manivel's name is sometimes mentioned as Manimekalai or Manikka Thirumalai in various Jaina texts.
historical_references.time_period: Sangam period (2nd century BCE to 4th century CE)
historical_references.context: Jaina author and contributor to Agama scriptures

historical_references.reference: Another Manivel, a Chola king who ruled from around 1110 to 1133 CE, is known for his military campaigns and temple construction. He is also referred to as Manivendra Pallavarayar or Manivendra Chola. During his reign, he extended the Chola empire to the northeast, conquering parts of present-day Odisha and Bengal. He built several temples, including the renowned Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram.

It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
